invariants.evidence: No second SWAP kernel or soil-water solver path is introduced.
Provider and evaluator modules contain no file, path, parsing or legacy I/O semantics.
Accepted water candidate, external thermal request/response, immutable enthalpy parameters and energy result are separate types.
External request/response metadata is evaluation-scoped and not added to persistent continuation state.
Requests, responses and energy accumulation are call-local and suitable for worker-local execution.
The seam is a narrow logical API and does not prescribe per-column object-heavy storage; later batching remains possible.
The evaluator consumes an already materialized candidate; provider responses cannot authorize acceptance or commit.
External binding requires no repeat Richards or soil-temperature solve and can be re-evaluated from the same candidate.
Request time coordinates are generic t0/t1 and current-reference quadrature uses sample t1 without calendar assumptions.
No fixed day or midnight coupling-window assumption is introduced.
The provider seam is explicitly runtime/coupler-facing and candidate-scoped; publication remains a separate transaction step.
Direct groundwater H/q interface convention and residual authority remain untouched.
Only candidate Q enters energy algebra; provider response contains no replacement water transfer.
No interface-sensitivity contract is changed.
Provider binding is O(external accepted samples) and adds zero SWAP physical solves.
Procedure seam can be backed by batch-aware runtime composition without one heavy solver instance per column.
No MODFLOW cell identity or tile fraction appears in either production module.
Deep-vadose may supply an external temperature through an adapter but remains outside SWAP state and routing.
Thermal metadata cannot create, destroy or duplicate water; transition mass remains external authority.
Any soil-water solver producing the public accepted bottom carrier can use the same evaluator/provider seam.
Existing EB-I04 enthalpy law, EB-I13 carrier and EB-I15 evaluator behavior are reused.
No HeadCalc or Richards-internal array dependency exists.
External donor temperature is physical metadata; provider batching/caching remains execution policy and cannot change the physics contract.
No unbounded retry or reconstruction path is added; invalid/unavailable provider states fail immediately and diagnostically.
Legacy EB-I15 fail-closed entrypoint remains available as the reference behavior without external capability.
Result counters distinguish complete, unavailable, stale, invalid and identity-mismatched external responses.
Provider is never called for local-outflow or exact-zero samples; unused functionality incurs no per-column state cost.
External source mapping remains outside SWAP; production modules contain no source-system-specific type.
No implicit .swp, daily start, MODFLOW presence or source identity assumption exists.
This audit and the qualification gate explicitly test all thirty architecture invariants for the workunit.
